title: Design a Payment System: idempotency keys, double-spend prevention, two-phase payment (authorize → capture), refund handling, ledger/audit trail, PCI compliance.
keyPoints: Idempotency keys make retries safe: the server stores results by key so a replay returns the same outcome.
Double-spend prevention uses atomic conditional updates or optimistic locking so two requests cannot both spend the last rupee.
Two-phase authorize-then-capture reserves funds first, then settles later, matching card network flows.
Refunds are new ledger entries, not edits to old ones, preserving the append-only audit trail.
The ledger is append-only double-entry: every transaction writes a debit and matching credit so the sum is always zero.
PCI DSS compliance means never storing raw card numbers; tokenize through a compliant vault.
A reconciliation job detects mismatches between the gateway and the local ledger and repairs them.

s1_definition.oneliner: Make payments idempotent, prevent double-spend with atomic checks, authorize before capture, and record every movement in an append-only double-entry ledger.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Idempotency key** : a client-generated unique id per payment so retries return the same result instead of double-charging.
- **Double-spend prevention** : atomic conditional update or optimistic locking ensuring the same balance is not committed twice.
- **Two-phase (authorize-capture)** : authorize reserves funds; capture settles them. Uncaptured auths can be voided.
- **Double-entry ledger** : every transaction writes a debit and a matching credit; the signed sum is always zero.
- **PCI DSS** : the system never stores raw card numbers; it tokenizes through a compliant vault.
s1_definition.analogy: When Rajesh pays Priya for rent through National Bank of India, the bank first checks and reserves the money (authorize), then actually moves it (capture). If Rajesh's phone retries because the network blinked, the bank recognizes the same payment and does not charge twice. Every rupee movement is written in a permanent ledger with two entries : money out and money in.

sections.s6_takeaway:
A payment system moves money with correctness, durability, and auditability as its highest priorities. Idempotency keys make retries safe. Double-spend prevention uses atomic conditional updates. Two-phase authorize-then-capture matches card network flows. The append-only double-entry ledger ensures every debit has a matching credit and the books always balance.

PCI compliance means never storing raw card numbers. A reconciliation job repairs mismatches between the gateway and local ledger. At National Bank of India, this combination of mechanisms made the payment system trustworthy enough to move real money.

Remember one sentence: make payments idempotent, prevent double-spend atomically, use authorize-capture for funds reservation, and record everything in an append-only double-entry ledger.
